reported.title: Relay chatters because firmware has no hysteresis or filtering
reported.description: The control logic at lines 66-73 uses a single trip point (FAN_ON_C = 42.0, line 8) with no lower OFF threshold and no hysteresis band, so any temperature sample below 42.0 immediately turns the fan off. Combined with the unfiltered per-sample read at line 56 (every 50 ms, line 10), sensor noise around the threshold flips the relay on every sample. Measured evidence confirms this: D8 toggled 57 times in a 5000 ms window starting at 900 ms (limit 2), 34 times in the rapid-oscillation scenario, and 8 times for a single glitch spike, all far exceeding the 2-toggle limit. D8 toggled 57 times in a 5000 ms window starting at 900 ms (limit 2), and 77 times over the whole 8.00 s run.

judge_input.spec:
- LM35 temperature probe on A0 scaled at 10 mV/°C; ridge-vent relay on D8; override pushbutton on D3 to ground with internal pull-up (active LOW).
- Turn the vent fan ON when attic temperature reaches 42.0 °C or above, and turn it OFF when temperature falls to 38.0 °C or below.
- While D3 is held LOW, force the fan ON regardless of temperature.
- Fan must not change state more than 2 times in any 5000 ms window.
- Print one status line every 1000 ms in the form `attic: <temp> C fan=ON` or `attic: <temp> C fan=OFF` with temperature to one decimal place.
- Reach the commanded fan state within 500 ms of a sustained threshold crossing.
